literal: Virtue he does not speak, non-virtuous things even if he does, a person, behind one's back he does not speak, to say is sweet.
translation: Even if a person does not speak of virtue and commits acts of vice, it is still a redeeming good if it can be said of him, 'he does not speak ill of others behind their backs.'
modern: ஒருவன் அறவழிகளைப் பேசாமல், பாவங்களையே செய்தாலும் கூட, அவன் 'பிறரைப் புறங்கூற மாட்டான்' என்று பிறர் சொல்வது அவனுக்கு நன்மையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme gravity of backbiting by comparing it with other vices. Even if a person fails to speak of virtuous things and actively commits sinful deeds, there is still a saving grace if others can say of him that he never speaks ill of anyone behind their back. The word 'இனிது' (sweet or good) indicates that avoiding backbiting is so valuable that it brings a redeeming goodness to an otherwise flawed character. The poet emphasizes that backbiting is a vice so destructive that abstaining from it is a great virtue in itself.
